props.title: Maid in Manhattan

sections.content: Maid in Manhattan (2002) exemplifies the early 2000s romantic comedy renaissance, following the Cinderella template that dominated the genre. Jennifer Lopez plays Marisa Ventura, a hotel maid mistaken for a wealthy guest by senatorial candidate Chris Marshall (Ralph Fiennes). The film shares DNA with Working Girl (1988) and Pretty Woman (1990), exploring class dynamics in Manhattan's luxury hotels and penthouses. Director Wayne Wang, known for The Joy Luck Club (1993), brings subtle commentary on immigrant experiences and social mobility to what could've been a purely commercial venture.

sections.content: The film sparked a wave of hospitality industry-set romantic comedies, including Hotel for Dogs (2009) and The Proposal (2009). Lopez's performance cemented her rom-com queen status, leading to Monster-in-Law (2005) and The Wedding Planner (2001). The film's examination of class barriers and social appearances resonates with earlier classics like Sabrina (1954) and its 1995 remake, though with a distinctly multicultural New York perspective. SUBHEAD: Class and Identity in Modern Rom-Coms

Wang's direction elevates standard rom-com tropes through authentic New York locations and genuine chemistry between Lopez and Fiennes. The service industry backdrop anticipates later works like Overboard (2018) and Crazy Rich Asians (2018), where class differences drive both conflict and comedy. Stanley Tucci and Natasha Richardson deliver sharp supporting performances that ground the fantasy in workplace reality.
